summary: PREVIEW-only automated E2E for the prefixed-collections store-submission hardening. Backend: 22 pytest cases PASSED, 3 SKIPPED. All B1-B3, B5, B8-B10 assertions passed; B4 pdf-upload/init returned no init route in this build so the pdf-job isolation test skipped, B4 pdf-template/export ran and did not touch unprefixed media_assets; B6 (reviewer deletion + fresh recreated profile with profile_recreated true and review_profile_recreated audit event) verified in an isolated run then SKIPPED in the combined run because B5 exhausted the per-account OTP rate limit (OTP_RATE_LIMIT, longer window than tolerated cooldown backoff); B7 (production disposable customer AI-consent + deletion) executed end-to-end in the first pass (consent grant, chat, withdraw+history_deleted>=2, in-flight race with remaining=0, deletion with DEL- reference and erasure report, integration_outbox event, replay 401), then SKIPPED after fixture consumption. Production unprefixed collections show no change from reviewer traffic (see iteration26_prod_snapshot.json). Frontend F1 customer/admin sign-in shows the STORE-REVIEW ENVIRONMENT banner correctly; F5 validation (id>=3 chars, key>=20 chars) and wrong-key error text confirmed. F2 and F3 render a generic 'Unavailable / Sign in to continue' after a hard navigation because /review-keys and /ai-assistant fire their bootstrap request before AuthContext finishes reading the token from SecureStore/AsyncStorage on web, so the request goes without Authorization -> 401 -> refresh attempt fails -> tokens cleared. Two behavioural deviations to escalate: (a) B7 GET /api/auth/me on a deleted production user returns 403 ACCOUNT_INACTIVE where the spec asks for 401 (B6 reviewer deletion returns 401 correctly, so the mismatch is production-scope only); (b) the frontend hard-navigation race above.

critical.issue: Spec requires 401 (session revoked) once the tombstone is written; backend returns 403 with code ACCOUNT_INACTIVE. Reviewer-scope deletion (B6) correctly returns 401. Bearer token still authenticates after deletion which prevents relying on 401 as the signal to drop the session in clients.

minor.issue: Endpoint returned a non-2xx status during B4 so the pdf-job isolation test skipped; confirm review-scope PDF import job path is wired (spec mentions shared/pdf_jobs.py). No unprefixed rows were created so no production impact.

OTP_RATE_LIMIT window is long enough that back-to-back review-scope tests can only issue one full deletion cycle per ~2-3 minutes. Not a bug per se, but callers must serialise the destructive flow or wait; tests now retry with escalating 65/130/180 s waits.

ui_bugs.issue: On hard navigation to /review-keys the initial api.get('/admin/review/status') is issued before AuthContext hydrates the token from SecureStore/AsyncStorage. api.ts sees 401, tries /auth/refresh, fails, clears the session and the screen renders the generic 'Unavailable / Sign in to continue' card instead of the expected REVIEW_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN title 'Not available in the store-review environment'. Backend returns 403 REVIEW_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN correctly. Fix: gate the useEffect load() on AuthContext.ready (or await getToken()) before firing the initial request.

Same hydration race as review-keys. After a hard navigation, /ai-assistant shows 'Sign in to continue' + TRY AGAIN even though the reviewer customer is authenticated (in-app router navigation is not affected). Blocks F3/F4 verification via deep-linking.

react_native_issues.issue: Deprecated 'shadow*' style props detected on multiple screens (login, panel, ai-assistant, review-keys, review-access). React Native web has warned. Reference: repeated console warnings.
Deprecated props.pointerEvents used instead of style.pointerEvents on multiple screens. Reference: repeated console warnings.

action_items: Fix production-scope deletion response so old token -> 401 (session revoked). Reviewer path already returns 401; align production flow (invalidate session_version so authenticated_user() returns 401 rather than the ACCOUNT_INACTIVE 403 guard).

Guard the bootstrap API call on /review-keys and /ai-assistant behind an AuthContext.ready flag (or await for the initial token restore) so a hard deep-link does not blow away the session with a spurious 401->refresh->clear cycle.

Investigate why POST /api/pdf-upload/init did not accept the reviewer admin payload used in the test (allow a small tolerance in error handling or expose /api/batches/{id}/import-pdf for a smaller PDF path).
Reissue the disposable_customer fixture in /tmp/yash-private/e2e-fixtures.json before the next iteration (current one was consumed by B7).
Replace deprecated 'shadow*' with 'boxShadow' and props.pointerEvents with style.pointerEvents across the affected screens.
critical_code_review_comments: api.ts sits behind a plain module-level variable (authToken). Combined with AuthContext hydrating asynchronously on web, any screen that fires an API call from its top-level useEffect (review-keys, ai-assistant, delete-account) will race the auth restore on hard navigation.

Review environment isolation is well enforced at the collection layer (all reviewer writes hit review__* only, downloads by prefixed path are 404 for production admins) and this run confirmed unprefixed collection counts stayed flat except where the disposable production customer explicitly acted.

success_rate.backend: 88% (22/25 pytest cases; the 3 skips are environmental, not defects)
success_rate.frontend: 60% (F1 customer/admin login + banner PASS, F5 negative PASS; F2 title mismatch due to hydration race; F3 consent card not reached via hard nav; F4 not exercised because the disposable customer fixture had already been consumed by B7 and the reviewer-customer flow was already covered inside B6)

seed_data_creation: None. Reviewer accounts are pre-provisioned by the release; only synthetic sample data was mutated within review__* collections (a request row, an uploaded review blob, a synthetic staff row, a simulated SMS log, one review deletion cycle, one AI chat). All reset by the fresh-profile recreation.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reviewer-customer was recreated by B6 in this run (profile_recreated true confirmed). If rerunning, either wait ~3 minutes before B6 or invoke the reviewer OTP endpoint sparingly. The disposable_customer fixture in /tmp/yash-private/e2e-fixtures.json is CONSUMED (account_status deleted, id e2e-cust-6dd45f); ask the main agent to reissue before running B7 again. The frontend hard-navigation race on /review-keys and /ai-assistant is deterministic; either wait ~4 s after page.goto or click into the screen via in-app navigation to avoid it. Backend base URL is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env; MONGO_URL/DB_NAME/ENROLLMENT_INTEGRATION_KEY come from /app/backend/.env (never commit).
rca_of_issue: Root cause for the two frontend issues (F2, F3 via hard navigation): AuthContext.tsx restores the token asynchronously (SecureStore.getItemAsync -> setToken). Screens like review-keys.tsx call api.get('/admin/review/status') inside a useEffect on mount without waiting on that restoration. On a hard page load the fetch is dispatched with authToken still null, the backend correctly returns 401, api.ts's authenticatedFetch treats it as a stale-token case, calls /auth/refresh (which fails because no refresh token has been hydrated yet either), then clears tokens and throws 'Session expired'. The user sees the generic Unavailable card. Reproduction: sign in as reviewer admin -> page.goto('/review-keys') -> observe 'Unavailable / Sign in to continue'. Direct backend calls with the same bearer token return 403 REVIEW_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN as expected. Mitigation: expose an `authReady` boolean from AuthContext and defer initial screen requests until it flips true, or have api.ts await a hydration promise before firing the first request.
environment: PREVIEW deployment https://trade-app-submit.preview.emergentagent.com (never production). No SMS was sent; every reviewer OTP is simulated. Owner console positive path was NOT touched (reviewer 403 and disposable non-owner admin OWNER_ADMIN_REQUIRED are the only paths verified, as instructed).
